ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In April 2015, scientists, through the European Space Agency astronomical telescope, discovered in an extragalactic galaxy a pair of supermassive binary black hole systems rotating around each other, as shown in the figure. This was also the first time astronomers discovered supermassive binary black holes in a normal galaxy. This has very important significance for verifying cosmology and galaxy evolution models, the applicability of general relativity under extreme conditions, and so on. At the end of this year, our country will also launch the dark matter detection satellite with the strongest functions in the world. If the masses of the binary black holes in the figure are respectively $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$, and they make uniform circular motion with a certain point on the line connecting the two as the center of the circle, according to the knowledge learned, which of the following options is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The ratio of the orbital radii of the binary black holes is $r_{1}:r_{2}=M_{2}:M_{1}$
